title: Batch Sculptor: per-workload temporal batching profiles and safe rollout
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a 'Batch Sculptor' service that continuously synthesizes lightweight, per-workload batching profiles using temporal decay, burst smoothing, and cache-awareness. The service will propose safe parameter changes and a guarded apply/rollback flow to minimize customer impact while reducing token cost.
background: Current global batching knobs are conservative and one-size-fits-all. Customers with steady request patterns are leaving cost on the table while bursty tenants suffer latency spikes when aggressive batching is applied. Previous work produced static profile recommenders; this ticket aims to operationalize continuous, time-aware profiles with a deterministic safe-apply path.
goals: Continuously generate candidate batching configurations per workload (tenant/route) with temporal smoothing
Prioritize cache-aware configs that leverage prefix/KV cache to reduce effective token work
Provide a deterministic safe-apply process: shadow-apply -> canary -> metrics gate -> automatic rollback
Expose audit trail and explainability for each recommended change
Ship integration with Console rollout UI and runtime for one-month pilot
proposal_summary: Introduce a new lightweight microservice 'batch-sculptor' that consumes workload fingerprints from the workload telemetry pipeline, runs a set of heuristics (latency-cost tradeoff, burst-smoothing, cache hit correlation), and outputs candidate profiles. Candidates are validated via an offline simulator and a shadow-apply stage that measures real-world effects without committing. A canary stage with SLO gates triggers a controlled apply; failures trigger automated rollback and postmortem entry.
design_decisions: Store per-workload profiles in KV store (etcd) with versioned diffs so rollbacks are deterministic
Use exponential temporal decay (alpha=0.2 default) to emphasize recent behavior while retaining history
Simulate candidate config impact in offline workload-replay using sampled KV/cache state from the last 72h
Guarded apply pipeline: shadow-apply (10% synthetic traffic) -> canary (5% real traffic) -> progressive ramp to 100% with metric gates
Expose human review flag for any candidate that changes max_batch_size by >50% or that reduces latency P95 by >20% at cost of >15% throughput drop
implementation_tasks: Telemetry: add workload fingerprint fields to workload-telemetry pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/312)
Microservice: implement batch-sculptor service with candidate generator and simulator
Runtime integration: accept profile diffs via /profiles API and support shadow-apply mode
Console: add Rollout type 'batching-profile' with review/approve UI and audit trail
E2E tests: replay-based simulator tests and chaos tests for safe-apply/rollback path
Docs: PRD and operator runbook in Confluence and quickstart guide in Drive
progress_updates: 2026-03-02 - Asha Patel: Spiked candidate generator prototype using k-means on inter-arrival time and sequence length. Early results show potential 12-18% token savings for steady workloads (offline sim).
2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Added KV/cache correlation metric to telemetry (telemetry PR #312). Verified cache hit-rate increases when conservative batching is applied on synthetic traces.
2026-03-07 - Design review: Sofia Martinez reviewed UI wireframes for Rollout page. Feedback: require clearer 'explainability' tooltip per candidate and explicit risk-level badge.

2026-03-10 - Engineering sync: Implemented shadow-apply path in runtime (runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823). Shadow-apply now collects delta metrics but does not alter production routing.

2026-03-12 - QA: Started offline replay runs against 72h sample corpus. Found one instability where extremely bursty traffic caused simulator to underpredict latency tail; added burst-smoothing heuristic to candidate generator.
testing_plan: Offline simulation using 72h sampled traces plus synthetic microbursts. Shadow-apply run for 48h on non-critical tenant namespace followed by 24h canary on low-traffic customers. Automated assertions: latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, token-per-inference, and cache-hit delta. Include chaos scenario that drops 25% of GPUs to validate rollback triggers.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal dev-only rollout to 'dev' cluster, 1 week
Stage 1: Shadow-apply enabled on staging, run candidate generation + simulator validation, 1 week
Stage 2: Canary apply to <5% of traffic for selected low-risk tenants with SLO gates, 2 weeks
Stage 3: Progressive ramp for pilot set (20 tenants), monitor for 2 weeks
Stage 4: Postmortem and policy tweaks, then wider opt-in pilot via Console (opt-in), 4 weeks
monitoring_and_alerts: Create Grafana dashboard 'Batch Sculptor - Candidate Impact' tracking token rate, cost per token, latency P95, cache-hit-rate per workload
SLO gates: rollback if P95 latency increases >10ms AND error rate increases >0.1% within 15m window
Alerting: PagerDuty on rollback triggers (severity P1); slack notification to #batch-sculptor for each candidate apply
Audit: Log profile diffs and simulator reports in S3 path s3://redwood-inference/batch-sculptor/audit/
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive batching yields cost savings but can harm tail latency for bursty tenants. We intentionally bias candidate selection toward cache-aware changes first. Long-term: integrate with per-tenant SLO profiles and biz-tier controls.
